Just now

--

It danced across the pale apricot sky, a kite lost in its own rhythm, shifting from side to side.
It wasn’t just paper; it wanted to be a bird,
Hunting for truth in the clouds that deceived the eye — heavy with promise, but hollow inside.
But dusk fell, and it was time to go home.
The string had to be cut, releasing the wanderer.
And still, I see it in my sleep sometimes…..
A bird that never stopped flying.
I remember watching this video as a kid where older people laughed stepping into a puddle of water, reminiscing about their good old times. It said, “Don’t kill the kid in you.” I took an oath that day: no matter what, I will never stop being the kid. I took everything for granted and never let the colors slip away. Every person was my friend: the sad bus conductor, the broken beggar, and my angry teachers. I used to imitate the Maneki-Neko cat and believed my Beyblade had powers. My parents were my gods and the elders my gurus.
Every day I woke up with enthusiasm to see if the pigeons’ eggs hatched. Until one day, a cat ate the pigeon and dragged the bloodied bodies onto the other balcony. I was eating my Chocos before going to school that day when I watched the light slip away from the bird’s eye. The eggs did hatch, but it was me who walked out of them. Yet I chose not to let go of the oath. I became the cat that killed the bird.
My curiosity took me places, but the destination was always that place. I turned around and took different routes, but I always reached the same spot. A black hole that never ends. I stared at it for too long until it gazed back, calling out to me. Before I jumped in, a mask approached that stuck to my face; like venom, it took over my body until I fell and kept falling. Times changed, homes changed, schools changed. Suddenly, there weren’t phone booths anymore.
There was another person inside me, a flayed baby in limbo that was always scared. He never talked nor fought. He was like water that took the shape of everything it touched just to be noticed. We used to talk only after midnight until the outsiders discovered him. It turned into a horror story when it was supposed to be Tom and Jerry. The whole town got frightened by this ghost, or was the town in my head? Everywhere I went, all I could see were those wolf eyes tracing my every step. Every Bus i took i could feel the hands on flesh that didn’t belong to me anymore. The God did use his weapons to bring me back to reality. I couldn’t run without legs, so I became a slave to it all. I bowed down before the one I served to get what I deserved.
One day the cat died. The watchman took him away from my floor’s corridor, walked across the street, and slit its throat. I waited the whole evening, yet the bowl of milk never dried up. My Mystique never returned. Maybe curiosity killed him, learning about a world that functioned on pain. Darkness at every junction, I chose green. Yet I never forgot the oath. The stones I worshipped turned out to be stones, dry and broken like the rest.
I begged, “Master, Master, where’s the dreams that I’ve been after? Master, Master, you promised only lies.” Now I was free, but the flayed baby in me took over and I became the audience. He played the role better. I clapped as I watched like the coach that trained him. He was an unfinished mirror that took glass from everyone to complete himself. He came for me one day with his white knife. The oath was a lie i kept telling myself all along.
I still dream of him, the man on the moon.
